#### 20.4.2 Six-relation closure, exact scope, and the hold lock

The runner's complete declared read closure is exactly
`(erasure_requests, deterministic_calculations, runs, human_gates, legal_holds,
document_artifacts)`. It may read no other durable relation. The exact read projections are:

- `erasure_requests(request_id,tenant_id,deal_id,status)` for the locked request and the closed
  executable state set `REQUESTED|FAILED`;
- `deterministic_calculations(tenant_id,deal_id,calc_id)`, `runs(tenant_id,deal_id,run_id)`, and
  `human_gates(tenant_id,deal_id,gate_id)` for the only approved indirect deal joins for
  `calc_sanads`, `run_steps`, and `human_gate_actions`, respectively;
- `document_artifacts(tenant_id,deal_id,doc_id,uri)` for the selected deal's exact document IDs
  and persisted `idis://` artifact-key projection; and
- `legal_holds(tenant_id,target_type,target_id,lifted_at)` for active `DEAL`, `DOCUMENT`, and
  `ARTIFACT` holds over the selected deal and that projection.

An unexpected or malformed artifact locator makes hold resolution fail closed; it is never
silently excluded from the census. Every CURRENT48 and frozen FUTURE38 DELETE statement contains
both exact tenant and deal scope bound to the callable's tenant/deal arguments. A direct target
uses its own `(tenant_id,deal_id)`. Each indirect child uses its own tenant and exact parent key
plus the corresponding declared parent's `(tenant_id,deal_id)`. Omission, weakening, a
tenant-only/delete-all shape, an undeclared parent, or a read outside the six-relation closure
fails SQL admission.

The shared lock contract is named `erasure-tenant-advisory-lock-v1`. Its only legal key
derivation is the literal, hash-bound SQL expression
`pg_catalog.hashtextextended('idis-task7-erasure-tenant-lock-v1:' || tenant_id::text, 0)`, and it
is acquired transaction-locally with `pg_catalog.pg_advisory_xact_lock`. The runner and every
durable legal-hold INSERT, UPDATE/lift, or DELETE acquire that tenant key before inspecting or
mutating hold state. Migration `0038` enforces the hold-write side for direct SQL as well as the
repository path; no session-scoped lock, caller-selected seed/key, advisory try-lock, or
unlocked durable mutation is admitted. A hold row cannot change tenant while passing this guard.

After establishing the canonical transaction-local tenant setting, the runner acquires the
tenant advisory lock, locks the exact request row, revalidates its request/tenant/deal/status,
rederives the complete deal/document/artifact target projection, and rejects any active matching
hold before setting `idis.erasure_context` or deleting. Two independent-connection tests prove
both races: (1) a hold writer that owns the lock and commits an active hold makes a waiting
erasure acquire the lock, observe the hold, and delete zero rows; and (2) an erasure transaction
that owns the lock prevents a concurrent hold write from completing until the erasure commits or
rolls back. Timeout, disconnect, or lock-acquisition failure is a hard failure with no deletion.

The 86-statement order is not accepted from a static list alone. A disposable PostgreSQL proof
materializes the reviewed current/future relation and constraint graph, adds the 14 derived
legacy targets, introspects the live foreign-key graph, and proves every child DELETE precedes
every reachable parent DELETE. The proof covers all 86 relations and names the three indirect
chains as mandatory witnesses: `run_steps -> runs`,
`calc_sanads -> deterministic_calculations`, and
`human_gate_actions -> human_gates`. It then executes the complete order against seeded legal
rows; any FK violation, absent relation, duplicate, omission, or parent-before-child edge fails
the disposable proof. Upgrade -> downgrade -> upgrade remains mandatory for migration `0038`.

#### 20.4.3 Executable least privilege and honest authority boundary

The SECURITY-DEFINER owner is least-privileged by direct and effective catalog proof. The fixed
NOLOGIN `idis_erasure_function_owner` owns both the runner and every Task-7 erasure append-only or
hold-lock helper; ownership may not differ. Its database grants are exactly:

- `USAGE` on the application schema, with no CREATE;
- SELECT on only the six read projections enumerated in section 20.4.2;
- predicate-column SELECT `(tenant_id,deal_id)` on every direct active target not already covered
  by those projections;
- predicate-column SELECT `(tenant_id,calc_id)` on `calc_sanads`, `(tenant_id,run_id)` on
  `run_steps`, and `(tenant_id,gate_id)` on `human_gate_actions`, matching their exact indirect
  predicates;
- DELETE on exactly CURRENT48 at migration `0038`, expanding to exactly RUNNER86 only in the
  approved FUTURE38 activation transaction; and
- column-limited `UPDATE(request_id)` on `erasure_requests`, solely because PostgreSQL requires
  UPDATE privilege on at least one selected column for `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`. The admitted
  function contains no UPDATE statement and cannot update any other column.

There is no INSERT, broader SELECT, broader UPDATE, TRUNCATE, schema-create, role membership,
SUPERUSER, or BYPASSRLS authority. The RED catalog matrix proves both direct and effective
privileges, proves UPDATE of `status`, `deal_id`, and every non-`request_id` column is denied, and
proves no membership supplies hidden rights. The fixed `idis_erasure_executor` is
`NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS`, has no standing table/schema-create privileges, and receives only
EXECUTE on the active runner. PUBLIC and the application role have no EXECUTE; readiness keeps
proving the application role cannot bypass ADMIN/audit composition.

The real composition proof runs the SECURITY-DEFINER body against disposable PostgreSQL with
canonical ENABLE+FORCE RLS. The owner is not exempt: the body uses the canonical transaction-local
tenant setting and the six-relation policies, never trigger disabling or BYPASSRLS. The erasure
marker is transaction-local, is set only after the locked request is revalidated in
`REQUESTED|FAILED` and the in-lock hold census is empty, and is not authority by itself. A valid
invocation deletes only the selected tenant/deal graph in complete child-first order. An unset,
forged, cross-tenant, cross-deal, held, or otherwise out-of-context invocation fails with zero
deletions, and the proof rechecks every target and retained authority row afterward.

The function proves request/status/hold state. ADMIN authorization, durable audit-before-call,
and use of the dedicated credential are deliberately enforced by API composition; the database
function does not claim to prove that entire cross-component sequence. The optional durable-audit
precondition was evaluated: current `audit_events.request_id` is TEXT and has no immutable
attempt-level FK/unique binding to the composite erasure request and retry attempt, while the

Downgrade of `0038` restores the exact `0037` guard/helper definitions and enable states, owners,

database objects after the refusal census passes. Upgrade -> downgrade -> upgrade proves those

### 20.5 Pre-freeze completion of the executable erasure bytes

The freeze audit was performed before any canonical v3 output was written. It found that the
execution row bound the active/future runner and ACL but did not yet bind the direct hold-write
guard, the retained legacy guard replacements/restoration, or an executable future replacement
choreography. Those omissions are artifact-admission failures, not migration details. The v3
field schema is completed RED-first with the following nine fields, inserted after the future
activation census and before the three RED-case tuples:

1. `hold_lock_contract_tuple`;
2. `guard_authority_contract_tuple`;
3. `legacy_guard_replacement_tuple`;
4. `hold_lock_upgrade_sql_utf8_hex_tuple`;
5. `hold_lock_downgrade_sql_utf8_hex_tuple`;
6. `legacy_guard_upgrade_sql_utf8_hex_tuple`;
7. `legacy_guard_downgrade_sql_utf8_hex_tuple`;
8. `future_activation_sql_utf8_hex_tuple`; and
9. `future_restoration_sql_utf8_hex_tuple`.

The hold-lock upgrade installs exactly one fixed-owner, PUBLIC-revoked, safe-search-path trigger
function and one ordinary enabled `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE` row trigger on
`public.legal_holds`. The function selects `OLD.tenant_id` for DELETE and `NEW.tenant_id`
otherwise, rejects an UPDATE whose tenant changes, proves the canonical transaction-local tenant
setting equals that coordinate, and unconditionally acquires the exact
`hashtextextended`/`pg_advisory_xact_lock` key before returning `OLD` or `NEW`. It contains no
`pg_locks` read, advisory unlock, try-lock, shared lock, session lock, caller-selected seed, or
dynamic SQL. Repository add/update/delete paths acquire the same lock explicitly before their
first mutation; the durable lift composition acquires it before reading and keeps its SELECT,
audit-before-write boundary, and UPDATE in one database transaction. The trigger makes any direct
SQL mutation transaction-locked rather than attempting to infer how the caller acquired a lock.
The downgrade tuple drops only that exact trigger and function, without `IF EXISTS` or CASCADE.

The legacy replacement census is closed over exactly seven function signatures and their retained
trigger catalog shapes:

- `public.idis_prevent_strict_preflight_proof_mutation()`;
- `public.idis_task5_selection_guard()`;
- `public.idis_task5_coverage_scope_guard()`;
- `public.idis_task6_erasure_requested(uuid,uuid)`;
- `public.idis_task6_immutable_guard()` and its eight immutable triggers;
- `public.idis_task6_attempt_guard()`; and
- `public.idis_task6_validate_result_outputs()` and both deferred result/output triggers.

Upgrade preserves each pre-`0038` function owner and ordinary trigger enable state, pins
`search_path=pg_catalog,pg_temp`, fully qualifies every application relation/helper, and routes
the DELETE exception through one new
`public.idis_task7_approved_erasure_context_v1(uuid,uuid)` SECURITY-DEFINER helper. That helper is
owned by the same NOLOGIN owner as the runner, revoked from PUBLIC, and returns true only for the
dedicated executor, fixed current owner, exact transaction-local tenant, exact true erasure
marker, and a same-tenant/deal `REQUESTED|FAILED` request. Replacement guards short-circuit on
the principal pair before invoking the ungranted helper, preserving the normal app-role failure
surface. The deferred validator recognizes that same authenticated DELETE before reading parents
that the runner has already deleted. The runner brackets all DELETEs with literal
`SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED` and `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE`, so every deferred check is
forced while the SECURITY-DEFINER owner and transaction-local context are still active.

Downgrade replays the literal canonical `0031`, `0036`, and `0037` function bytes and their pinned
SHA-256 values, restoring empty function proconfig and leaving the exact original owners and
ordinary enabled trigger definitions intact, then drops only the new context helper. The
upgrade/downgrade catalog proof compares function body, owner, security mode, proconfig, trigger
events/orientation/deferrability/enabled state, ACL, and dependencies before upgrade, after
upgrade, after downgrade, and after the second upgrade.

The `0031` source function has three line comments inside its dollar-quoted PL/pgSQL body. The
canonical one-line restoration strips only those comments before whitespace normalization;
otherwise the first `--` would consume the rest of the function body and the supposedly exact
downgrade would not compile. The admitted executable statement SHA-256 is
`1a05ce8af35fe5102cba13e3198cdf92e82b966a15ea88552024fc7244c7e139`. The pre-freeze
non-executable normalization SHA-256
`936e51dc99b3e149216dfe9ec471597753aa40e42967ea718e18f855ff3174d4` is retained only in
this narrative as rejected evidence and must not occur in the normative artifact or fixture.
The other six legacy restoration hashes remain byte-identical.

The frozen future activation tuple equals exactly `DROP FUNCTION <exact runner signature>`, the
literal RUNNER86 CREATE body, and the complete future reset ACL. The inverse tuple equals the
same exact DROP, the literal CURRENT48 CREATE body, and the complete current reset ACL. The DROP

The FUTURE38 table-creating migration may execute the activation tuple only after rederiving the

These additions leave all semantic, route, extractor, provider, relation-count, and erasure-order

### 20.6 Post-freeze semantic rejection and pending v4 ruling

The one-shot materializer produced the append-frozen v3 artifact at SHA-256
`b2cf25203e7c3998fc3d616a488e3634665ab66a642be998365cc5380893e9d0`; the generated fixture is

`498fdc8b2edb12dacaaca65ffd98da7c096c9f4d8109f1f1bee1319b25ebc1c4`. All 25 section hashes,
the `28/47/1,756/19` registry counts, the `48/38/86` erasure split, the 72-relation/66-phase
erasure census, the 64-table RLS inventory, and the unchanged semantic/route/extractor vectors
rederived successfully. These facts prove byte determinism; they do not cure semantic defects.

The post-freeze audit found three blocks-live defect classes in those immutable bytes:

1. Both frozen erasure bodies reject only a non-null malformed `document_artifacts.uri`. Migration
   `0004` defines that field nullable, so a selected null locator is silently absent from the
   artifact-key/hold projection even though section 20.4.2 requires every unexpected locator to
   fail closed. The RED contract requires the invalid-locator predicate to include
   `a.uri IS NULL OR a.uri NOT LIKE 'idis://%' OR a.uri='idis://'` before any erasure mutation.
2. `dashboard-root-equation-v1` incorrectly requires `required_calculations` to be non-empty and
   then proves only one existential calculation witness. Empty arrays are legal and mean none
   required: 20 of 21 frozen CDD questions use `[]`, and the FDD importer returns an empty tuple for
   every sheet except P&L and Cash Flow. For a future frozen question containing two required
   calculation types, one matching calculation also incorrectly satisfies the existential test.
   The approved equation requires empty-array-as-false semantics (including a false-valued
   `bool_or` result for an empty set) and a per-required-type anti-join proving every `required=true`
   type has its scoped calculation lineage before exact root-link equality is evaluated.
3. E029 selects every persisted HIT fact using only provider, fact domain, parent outcome, and
   output kind, then unconditionally derives both `GRAPH_EVIDENCE:external_context` and
   `RAG_EVIDENCE:external_context` expectations. The separately approved Task-9 contract keeps a
   rights-restricted HIT fact durable but removes both Graph and RAG intents/edges when
   `rag_index_allowed=false`; its composition test passes in the declared environment. The frozen
   Task-7 future outcome/fact shapes persist rights hashes but no immutable indexability decision,
   so three-way equality can never hold for that legal Task-9 branch. Silently dropping the fact,
   manufacturing Graph/RAG receipts, or treating a rights denial as provider N/A would each
   violate an already approved contract. The proposed V4 ruling preserves Task-9 semantics and
   adds `external_context_index_allowed BOOLEAN NOT NULL` to the immutable provider-outcome tuple,
   sourced exactly from Task-9 admission's `rag_index_allowed` decision and bound into the outcome,
   native-output, rights-lineage, and rehydration hashes. E029 then retains only its unconditional
   non-index consumers; new E048 selects facts whose parent HIT outcome has that exact value true
   and emits exactly the Graph and RAG routes. E030 remains unconditional. This changes the edge
   rule count `47 -> 48`, changes E029's equation from `sum((8+a_p)*fact_count)` to
   `sum((6+a_p)*fact_count)`, adds E048 as `2*sum(index_allowed*fact_count)`, and preserves the
   static 1,756-route count by moving the existing 50 Graph/RAG routes from E029 to E048. The
   selector/rule/hash-vector deltas and the exact false/true/restart/finalization RED cases are
   pending explicit reviewer approval; the alternative of suppressing durable facts when indexing
   is denied is rejected because it contradicts the approved Task-9 contract.

The two artifact-level failing tests are
`test_current_and_future_runners_fail_closed_on_null_or_malformed_artifact_uri` and

6. ordering of object deletion, database deletion, terminal audit, and request-state/count

The callable currently returns exact deletion counts but the approved ACL grants its owner only

Before deleting, the function proves one and only one valid open attempted event for the exact
request/tenant/deal and ADMIN actor, verifies its deterministic event identity/hash and
ordinal/prior chain, locks and revalidates a REQUESTED-or-FAILED request, rechecks legal holds
under the shared tenant advisory lock, rederives the bound object target-set digest, and requires
the staged `object_rows_reconciled` integer to equal the bound artifact-row count. The same
transaction deletes the current relation set, writes `EXECUTED`, actor, statement timestamp, and
the exact merged per-relation plus object-reconciliation counts, and returns those persisted
values. The future body carries the same semantics over RUNNER86 and remains frozen/inactive
until the existing FUTURE38 activation census.

Production orchestration uses one dedicated connection from the already-approved
`IDIS_ERASURE_DATABASE_URL`. It holds the existing deterministic tenant advisory lock at session
scope across locked rehydration, audit-validated target enumeration, bounded external object
reconciliation, and the short database-function transaction. After lock acquisition, request
state and lineage are reloaded through the application role. Target enumeration then uses a
separate short application-role/RLS transaction while the dedicated backend retains the session
lock. The dedicated role therefore keeps zero standing table privileges and issues only
lock/unlock plus the admitted function call. The composition does not hold a database transaction
open across external I/O and makes no cross-connection or cross-system ACID claim. Hold mutation
and the function continue to use the same deterministic lock key; the hold check runs after the
locked rehydration and before target enumeration or object mutation. Explicit unlock/close is
required; backend death releases the session lock.

Under the session lock, a short read transaction first enumerates and hashes the immutable target
set. The attempted event carrying that digest is then durable before any object mutation and
before the callable can satisfy its precondition. A failure before database commit writes the
deterministic failed terminal and retains its immediate lineage for the next ordinal. A crash
after the function commits but before the succeeded event leaves an
`EXECUTED` request with exact persisted counts and one open attempt. Retry detects that state
before the ordinary already-executed conflict, writes the same deterministic succeeded event
using the persisted `executed_at` and counts, and performs no object operation, function call,
delete, or recount. Deterministic event insertion is conflict-verifying: an identical existing
event is accepted as the same evidence; different bytes under the same event ID fail closed.

The middleware's generic `erasure.executed` event may be suppressed only for the exact
`executeErasureRequest` operation, exact POST execute path, and a route-set proof that the
Task-7 succeeded event is durable. Before suppression, tests prove field parity for actor,
tenant, deal, outcome, and timestamp. Every other mutation keeps its existing immutable audit
event; an execute response without replacement lineage fails closed. Exact validator admission
is limited to the three tabled Task-7 names, not a prefix.

When PostgreSQL is configured, the production route, app factory, default builder, and any
process-global override can select only the Task-7 dedicated composition. The legacy
`PostgresErasureExecutor` may remain as historical test code but has zero production reachability.
The in-memory twin is selectable only while PostgreSQL is absent. Static and real API/PostgreSQL
tests prove no production composition issues a CURRENT48 DELETE through the app role, the app
role cannot execute the callable, and neither legacy executor can be smuggled into the route.
Direct-SQL probes preserve the existing canonical RLS/guard contract rather than inventing a
blanket DELETE revocation.

All v19 census, readiness, migration, upgrade -> downgrade -> upgrade, direct-SQL, and
zero-mutation assertions execute as the application role except unavoidable administrative DDL
setup. The signed census separately proves dedicated-executor success without relabeling it as an
application-role case. Publication remains journaled fixture-first/artifact-last; migration
`0038` cannot consume v19 until the signed fixture and append-frozen artifact exist.

The Task-7 checkpoint boundary is also hash/report binding. Task 7 proves current schema, guards,
ACL, admission, derivation, and available producers. It cannot prove the complete 27 restart cuts
or all-48-rule three-way equality while FUTURE38 receipt relations and later producers are
absent. The exact producer-blocked rules, derived by intersecting producer-selector relation
tuples with the frozen future producer relations, are:

`E028_PROVIDER_OUTCOME_COMMON`,
`E029_PROVIDER_FACT_SEMANTIC`,
`E030_PROVIDER_FACT_DELIVERABLES`,
`E031_GRAPH_INTERNAL_DOWNSTREAM`,
`E032_RAG_INTERNAL_DOWNSTREAM`,
`E033_GRAPH_EXTERNAL_DOWNSTREAM`,
`E034_RAG_EXTERNAL_DOWNSTREAM`,
`E035_CONFLICT_INTERNAL_DOWNSTREAM`,
`E036_CONFLICT_EXTERNAL_DOWNSTREAM`, and
`E048_PROVIDER_FACT_EXTERNAL_CONTEXT`.

The prior real-PostgreSQL failure remains honest evidence:
`CONSUMER_RECEIPT_INCOMPLETE` at the first admitted E001/E002 paths because FUTURE38
`step_receipt_input_references` is absent. Task 11 must rederive the blocked inventory and prove
every one of the 48 rules at all 27 restart cuts with
derived expectations = persisted expectations = durable receipts. No Task-7 wording may claim
that proof, and no later task may mark it discharged before the Task-11 exit gate.

The execution sequence is: RED lineage/materialization/composition tests; deterministic v18 ->
v19 build and byte-exact inverse; complete application-role census plus dedicated-executor
supplement; signed authorization; atomic freeze; `0038` retargeting; app-role migration and
readiness proofs; product composition; focused, PostgreSQL, full-tree, and offline verification;
then the Task-7 checkpoint. No commit, push, PR, live call, priced call, activation, or future
table fabrication is authorized.

### 20.29 Approved full-strict-v20 erasure RETURNING-to-SELECT closure

V19 is preserved only as unfrozen historical derivation evidence and is permanently void:
candidate `21bb93882a2d316bbf899cdae282c231b99a1aeea2239c2966954bfa7f4789c4`,
prospective frozen
`91a6d99322d7c2dd8fba862db9d4fe858e89f933cc22c1e126fdb9c5ec1dd76b`,
and prospective contract
`47945b910257381adbf0b895d6596730762828592041c7bb1c4086bb5b25035b`.
It was never signed, frozen, fixture-published, migration-consumed, or runtime-selected.

The first v19 census failure was a composition omission: the separately reviewed ownership
statement for `public.idis_task7_approved_erasure_context_v1` was not installed before guarded
deletion. The helper ran under the setup administrator and the first guarded artifact delete
failed `TASK7_SOURCE_FREEZE_FENCED`. The census scaffold now composes helper ownership and its
read closure before installing the runner. This is a harness correction and changes no frozen
authority tuple.

The second failure was PostgreSQL's column-privilege rule for DML `RETURNING`. The runner
already atomically returned `status,executed_by,executed_at,counts`, while the reviewed owner
SELECT grant on `erasure_requests` omitted `executed_by` and `executed_at`. V20 adds exactly
those two SELECT columns in the current, future, activation, and restoration ACL copies. The
existing UPDATE grant remains exactly
`request_id,status,executed_by,executed_at,counts`; the runner body, deletion transaction,
persisted-count proof, audit chain, and crash reconstruction remain byte-identical.

The class fix is hash-bound as `task7-returning-select-closure-v1`. The generator parses the
current and future runner's exact simple-identifier `RETURNING` lists, parses the paired
function-owner column SELECT grants, and requires exact closure. It also proves the composed
activation/restoration ACL tails equal the authoritative future/current body-plus-ACL tuples.
Missing returned columns, unread extra grants, duplicate grants, `*`, expressions, aliases,
relation drift, or composed-copy drift fail
`TASK7_RETURNING_SELECT_CLOSURE_INVALID` before any fixture can exist.

The unfrozen v20 candidate is
`d046026da38b0eddbafc05368f43300b8c4aff7bfe0a8a9c1def0c960927f91a`.
Its semantic invariance wall is exact: 28 steps, 48 rules, 1,756 routes, 19 extractors,
18 providers, rights routing, current/future relation sets, table census, erasure ordering,
event/UUID vectors, RLS/role model, and every prior section 18/20.2 ruling are unchanged.
It remains `append_frozen=false`, unsigned, without a fixture, and unavailable to migration or
runtime until the complete application-role census, dedicated-executor supplement, signed
receipt, and atomic publication succeed.

The Task-7/Task-11 boundary from section 20.28 is unchanged. Task 7 proves schema, guards, ACL,
admission, deterministic derivation, and producers available now. Task 11 must still rederive
and discharge E028-E036 and E048 across every one of the 27 restart cuts with
derived expectations = persisted expectations = durable receipts.
